Maggie —

Appreciate the clear list. I attached a redline (redline_MSA_v3.pdf) with three focused options we typically offer:

Option A — Customer retains output ownership; Redwood gets a limited operational feedback license (non-derivative, anonymized) for service improvement unless explicit opt-in for training.
Option B — Customer retains output ownership; zero-training default (Redwood may process for routing/latency only); training allowed by explicit order form checkbox + addendum.
Option C — Customer grants a scoped feedback license that permits model improvements, with a 30-day data retention cap unless otherwise agreed.

Quick notes on the technical side (cc'ing Karthik for details):
- Opt-out for training means requests are tagged and excluded from the training pipeline; we also scrub logs forwarded to model-training clusters.
- We can enable prefix/KV caching on a per-tenant basis but do not persist prefixes for training when opt-out is selected.

Laura — can you suggest concrete contract wording (preferably short, redline-friendly) for the Order Form and a fallback MSA paragraph? Karthik — any operational caveats you'd add in a short note?

Connor / Maggie —

Below are two compact clause drafts we propose to put into the MSA (with an Order Form checkbox to select training behavior):

1) Customer Output. "Customer retains all right, title and interest in any content it inputs and any model outputs generated solely in response to Customer inputs ("Customer Output"). Redwood grants Customer a perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to use Customer Output for its business purposes."

2) Feedback & Training License (Order Form selectable):
"a) Operational Feedback: Unless the Order Form explicitly indicates 'No Operational Feedback', Customer agrees that Redwood may collect and use anonymous service telemetry and aggregated metrics for the purpose of improving service stability and performance. Such telemetry will not contain Customer identifiers or Customer Output in identifiable form.
b) Model Training: If the Order Form selects 'Allow Model Training', Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, transferable license to use de-identified Customer Input and Customer Output to improve Redwood models. Redwood will provide a 30-day retention window for raw logs used for training pipelines and will honor Customer's reasonable technical instructions to isolate prefixes and KV caches. If 'Allow Model Training' is not selected, Redwood will not use Customer Input or Customer Output to train models or include them in training datasets."

3) Audit & Verification: "Upon request and subject to a reasonable confidentiality agreement, Redwood will provide a description of data flows and a compliance attestation for the selected options."

I kept the language intentionally explicit and short so procurement lawyers can slot it in. If Acme needs a stricter carveout (example: no telemetry even as anonymized), we can prepare Option B as the default in the Order Form.

Quick operational addendum for the record —

- Tagging & Routing: We implement an account-level flag for training opt-out; any request with that flag is routed to an isolated path that excludes downstream training pipelines.
- KV/Prefix Handling: For opt-out seats, we persist KV cache for active sessions (to maintain latency) but we do not export those caches to training stores. We can also enable ephemeral-only KV (no disk persist) if Acme requires.
- Retention: Logs destined for training are TTL'd to 30 days by default; if training is disabled the logs are zero-retention for training clusters (still subject to debugging/incident retention windows, which we can limit contractually).
- Verification: We can provide a quarterly attestation and a one-time runbook review with Acme security to demonstrate isolation controls.

Operational caveat: If customer requests full zero-telemetry, that increases RPO for debugging incidents and may increase SLO variance. Open to discussing trade-offs.

-Karthik
